label: History
value: Billina was raised in the United States
unit: Billina was raised in the United States under her original name Bill until Dorothy Gale began calling her Billina. While visiting the Land of Ev, she was separated from Dorothy and confined in Princess Langwidere's chicken house, where she engaged in a fierce fight with a speckled rooster for dominance. After Dorothy released her, Billina joined Princess Ozma's party to the Nome King's underground palace. Because she alone knew the secret to identifying the transformed victims, she restored the Queen of Ev, five princesses, four princes, and Ozma back to their true forms. Following her adventures, she chose to live permanently in the Land of Oz, where she was granted emerald bracelets, a pearl necklace, and a life of comfort. Later, she hatched ten chicks, naming every single one of them Dorothy to make calling them easier.

label: History
value: The Braided Man was an inventor.
unit: While living on the surface of the earth, the Braided Man was an inventor who manufactured hole products, including holes for Swiss cheese and doughnuts. After inventing an adjustable post-hole, he stacked many together and accidentally fell down into the subterranean cavern inside Pyramid Mountain. He caught a projecting rock and established a small home and factory halfway up the mountain. There, he manufactured Assorted Flutters for flags and Rustles for silk gowns. When Dorothy Gale, the Wizard, and Zeb passed through his cave, he shared his story and offered them his products. Dorothy gave him a blue hair-ribbon for his braids, which made him very happy, and he insisted on giving them boxes of flutters and rustles in return. Later, he was invited to the Emerald City to attend Princess Ozma's birthday celebration, where he presented her with a box of flutters.

He caught a projecting rock and established a small home and factory halfway up the mountain. There, he manufactured Assorted Flutters for flags and Rustles for silk gowns. When Dorothy Gale, the Wizard, and Zeb passed through his cave, he shared his story and offered them his products. Dorothy gave him a blue hair-ribbon for his braids, which made him very happy, and he insisted on giving them boxes of flutters and rustles in return. Later, he was invited to the Emerald City to attend Princess Ozma's birthday celebration, where he presented her with a box of flutters.

label: History
value: Button-Bright was found sitting under a chestnut tree
unit: Button-Bright was found sitting under a chestnut tree along a remote road, steadily digging a hole with a piece of wood. When questioned by Dorothy Gale and the Shaggy Man, he could not explain where he lived or how he got there, leading them to realize he was lost. Because of the Shaggy Man's Love Magnet, Button-Bright willingly joined the party on their journey. Upon encountering the fox-soldiers of Foxville, his innocent questioning led the fox-captain to consider him clever, and he was brought before King Dox. During their travels, he was temporarily transformed into having a fox's head by King Dox before later having his true face restored at the Truth Pond. Along the way, he met Polychrome, the Daughter of the Rainbow, and eventually reached the Emerald City. In the royal palace, he was welcomed by Princess Ozma and Glinda the Good, assisted in winding up Tik-Tok, and enthusiastically attended Princess Ozma's royal birthday feast.

label: History
value: The Lion believed himself to be a coward.
unit: While living in the forest, the Lion believed himself to be a coward despite scaring away all men and beasts with his loud roar. Upon encountering Dorothy Gale, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and Toto, he decided to join their expedition to the Emerald City to ask the Great Oz for courage. Along the way, he formed a bond with Toto and accompanied the group through various perils. After falling asleep in a poisonous poppy field, he was rescued through the help of the field mice. Upon reaching the Emerald City and meeting the Wizard, he drank the contents of a square green bottle poured into a green-gold dish, which filled him with the courage he had sought.

label: History
value: Dorothy Gale hailed from a farm
unit: Dorothy Gale originally hailed from a farm in Kansas. During her travels, she became close friends with Princess Ozma of Oz, making her famous in fairy lands. On one journey, while traveling down a seventh road, she encountered a lost little boy named Button-Bright and took him under her care alongside Toto and the Shaggy Man. Upon arriving in Foxville, she held Toto to keep him from fighting the foxes, respectfully bowed before the Fox-King, and participated in the city's unique drum-pounding entrance ritual. In subterranean caverns, she stood her ground against young dragonettes tied to rocks, proudly defending her Kansas origins. Upon returning to Ozma's palace, she warmly embraced her old companions, including the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, while winding up Tiktok and searching for her lost hen Billina.

label: History
value: Eureka accompanied Dorothy Gale and her companions
unit: Eureka accompanied Dorothy Gale and her companions into subterranean realms beneath the Earth's surface after falling through an opening in California. Upon reaching the glass city of the Mangaboos, she discovered that the air could support her weight and amused herself by walking around on the air outside roof edges. She traveled alongside Dorothy, Zeb, Jim the Cab-Horse, and the Wizard through various underground caverns, using her superior night vision to detect hidden dragonettes. When the party was captured and held prisoner by the wooden Gargoyles, Eureka climbed down the stout wooden walls of their prison building to observe the creatures removing their wing hinges for sleep, which allowed the Wizard to devise a plan using their discarded wings to escape. After eventually arriving in the Land of Oz, Eureka was accused by the Woggle-Bug of murdering and eating one of Princess Ozma's nine tiny white piglets. She was placed on trial in the palace throne room, where the Tin Woodman defended her and the Hungry Tiger delivered a guilty verdict on behalf of the jury. Although the Tin Woodman produced a hidden piglet to save her, Eureka refused to accept freedom on false pretenses, exposing the trick and revealing what had actually become of Ozma's pet.

Upon reaching the glass city of the Mangaboos, she discovered that the air could support her weight and amused herself by walking around on the air outside roof edges. She traveled alongside Dorothy, Zeb, Jim the Cab-Horse, and the Wizard through various underground caverns, using her superior night vision to detect hidden dragonettes. When the party was captured and held prisoner by the wooden Gargoyles, Eureka climbed down the stout wooden walls of their prison building to observe the creatures removing their wing hinges for sleep, which allowed the Wizard to devise a plan using their discarded wings to escape. After eventually arriving in the Land of Oz, Eureka was accused by the Woggle-Bug of murdering and eating one of Princess Ozma's nine tiny white piglets. She was placed on trial in the palace throne room, where the Tin Woodman defended her and the Hungry Tiger delivered a guilty verdict on behalf of the jury. Although the Tin Woodman produced a hidden piglet to save her, Eureka refused to accept freedom on false pretenses, exposing the trick and revealing what had actually become of Ozma's pet.

label: History
value: Evardo was born.
unit: Evardo was born as the eldest prince of the royal family of Ev. His father, the King, sold Evardo, his mother, and his nine siblings to the Nome King, who placed them under magical enchantments as ornaments in his subterranean palace. Billina, the yellow hen, eventually discovered how to break the magic and restored Evardo and his family back to their original forms. Upon returning to Ev, his mother proclaimed him King Evardo Fifteenth before his cheering subjects on the palace balcony. Following his coronation, he awarded Billina a necklace of pearls and sapphires to express his gratitude. Later, Evardo accompanied his mother and royal siblings to the Land of Oz to attend Princess Ozma's birthday celebration, presenting her with a diadem of diamonds set in radium as a gift.

label: History
value: Glinda welcomed visitors to her palace.
unit: Glinda welcomed visitors to her beautiful palace in the South Country, including Dorothy Gale and later the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and their companions fleeing Jinjur's rebellion. Learning of the usurpation of the Emerald City, she investigated the mystery of the rightful royal heir. When Jinjur and the witch Mombi attempted to deceive her with transformations, Glinda led her army to the Emerald City and forced Mombi to reveal the truth. Using her magic white pearl, she detected Mombi's lies and uncovered that baby Princess Ozma had been transformed into the boy Tip. After overseeing Tip's restoration to Princess Ozma, Glinda launched a swift campaign using the flying Gump to capture Jinjur and restore peace. Following Princess Ozma's accession to the throne, Glinda continued to offer good advice to the young Queen.

label: Quotes
value: > Fat babies! Don't they sound delicious? But I've never eaten any, because my conscience tells me it is wrong. If I had no conscience I would probably eat the babies and then get hungry again, which would mean that I had sacrificed the poor babies for nothing. No; hungry I was born, and hungry I shall die. But I'll not have any cruel deeds on my conscience to be sorry for.

label: Quotes
value: > In that you are mistaken. I am a good beast, perhaps, but a disgracefully bad tiger. For it is the nature of tigers to be cruel and ferocious, and in refusing to eat harmless living creatures I am acting as no good tiger has ever before acted. That is why I left the forest and joined my friend the Cowardly Lion.

label: Quotes
value: > You have a good conscience, friend Horse, and if you attend to its teachings it will do much to protect you from harm. Some day I will let you try to crush in my skull, and afterward you will know more about tigers than you do now.

value: > Hush, Dorothy; you'll ruin my reputation if you are not more discreet. It isn't what we are, but what folks think we are, that counts in this world. And come to think of it Miss Polly would make a fine variegated breakfast, I'm sure.

value: The Hungry Tiger is a huge striped beast.

During ceremonial occasions, he wears a red ribbon bow tied on his tail.

label: Personality
value: The Hungry Tiger has a fierce appearance.
unit: Despite his fierce appearance and violent natural instincts, the Hungry Tiger possesses a strict conscience that prevents him from committing cruel acts or harming living creatures. He often expresses a desire to eat fat babies or small animals, but refrains because he refuses to suffer guilt or sacrifice innocent life for a temporary meal. While he considers himself a bad tiger for refusing to act cruelly, he is mild, polite, and deeply loyal to his friends. He is also mindful of his public image, humorously asking others to help protect his reputation as a fearsome monster.

label: History
value: Jack Pumpkinhead was created in the Country of the Gillikins.
unit: Jack Pumpkinhead was created in the Country of the Gillikins by Tip, who carved his limbs out of wooden sticks and fitted his body with a pumpkin head. He was brought to life after Mombi sprinkled him with the magic Powder of Life. After escaping with Tip, Jack traveled across the Land of Oz and met the Scarecrow in the Emerald City, with whom he quickly struck up a friendship and played games of quoits. He later joined Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, the Saw-Horse, and the Woggle-Bug on their various journeys, even sacrificing part of his wooden left leg to repair the Saw-Horse. Eventually, Jack settled down in a pumpkin field in Oz to work as a pumpkin farmer. Because his carved pumpkin head rots over time, Ozma routinely carves him fresh replacement heads, leading him to cultivate his own pumpkin patch to ensure he never runs out of spares. He hollowed out an extraordinarily large pumpkin in his patch to serve as his house, where he resides while preparing to attend Ozma's celebrations.

label: History
value: Jim was an old cab-horse.
unit: Jim was an old, overworked cab-horse belonging to Zeb who spent years pulling a public cab in Chicago before arriving at Hugson's Ranch. While waiting near Hugson's Siding, an earthquake struck, swallowing Jim, his attached buggy, Zeb, and Dorothy down a deep subterranean chasm. During the fall, Jim gained the ability to speak and safely landed on a glass roof. He drew the buggy carrying his companions through strange subterranean lands, grazing on grass in the Valley of Voe where he was warned about invisible bears. After enduring battles against Mangaboos and Gargoyles—where he used his iron-shod hoofs to kick attackers—he was fitted with wooden wings to help transport the group out of underground caverns. Upon arriving in the Land of Oz, Jim was treated with lavish respect as a guest in the Emerald City palace, given a green marble room, and fed uncooked oatmeal by palace servants. During a morning walk, he met the wooden Sawhorse, debating what constituted a 'Real Horse' before being terrified by the sudden arrival of the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger.

label: History
value: General Jinjur organized a secret rebellion
unit: General Jinjur organized a secret rebellion of four hundred young women from across Oz to overthrow the Scarecrow and seize the Emerald City. Along the road to the city, she encountered Tip, offered him food from her lunch basket, and drafted him to carry her packages. Upon reaching the green granite walls, she demanded the surrender of the Guardian of the Gate, stole his keys when her soldiers threatened him with knitting needles, and routed the unloaded Soldier with the Green Whiskers. By capturing the city without bloodshed, Jinjur established herself as Queen, took up residence in the royal palace, and allowed her troops to pry emeralds from the city streets. When Glinda the Good marched on the city to restore Princess Ozma, Jinjur barred the gates and issued a defiant refusal to surrender. However, Glinda's forces flew over the walls aboard the Gump, alighting directly in the palace courtyard where Jinjur was captured while lounging in a hammock. Following her defeat, Jinjur's army was disbanded, and she was released back to her home on a promise of good behavior.

label: History
value: When the Shaggy Man invoked the magic of the Love Magnet at the border of the Deadly Desert, Johnny Dooit instantly appeared.
unit: When the Shaggy Man invoked the magic of the Love Magnet at the border of the Deadly Desert, Johnny Dooit instantly appeared sitting atop a big copper chest while smoking a pipe. Upon learning that Dorothy Gale and her companions needed to cross the desert safely to reach the Emerald City, he immediately offered to build them a sand-boat. Unlocking his tool chest, he chopped down a tree, sawed it into broad boards, nailed the hull together, attached a mast, and rigged up a sail out of rope and canvas in just a few minutes while humming a cheerful song about work. Explaining how to sail the craft, he slammed down his tool chest lid and vanished into thin air before anyone could thank him. He was later expected to attend Princess Ozma's birthday celebration at the Emerald City Palace as an invited guest.

value: > Therefore, I will do you a great favor. I will confer upon you the head of a fox, so that you may hereafter look as bright as you really are.

value: > Don't mention Aesop to me, I beg of you! I hate that man's name. He wrote a good deal about foxes, but always made them out cruel and wicked, whereas we are gentle and kind, as you may see.

label: Quotes
value: > There is no question about our knowing more than men do. But we employ our wisdom to do good, instead of harm; so that horrid Aesop did not know what he was talking about.

label: Quotes
value: > But to become civilized means to dress as elaborately and prettily as possible, and to make a show of your clothes so your neighbors will envy you, and for that reason both civilized foxes and civilized humans spend most of their time dressing themselves.

unit: King Dox is proud, vain, and highly confident in the wisdom and civilization of his kind. He considers foxes to be gentle, kind, and far cleverer than human beings. He believes that civilization consists of dressing as elaborately as possible to make others jealous. He is also hospitable to guests, but can act impulsively with his magic when conferring animal transformations.

label: History
value: King Dox rules over the city of Foxville
unit: King Dox rules over the civilized city of Foxville as King Renard the Fourth. When Dorothy Gale, Button-Bright, the shaggy man, and Toto are brought into his city by his fox-soldiers, he receives them in his palace. Finding Button-Bright's answers remarkably clever, King Dox uses his magic to transform Button-Bright's human head into a fox head, later claiming he lacks the power to undo the change. He hosts the travelers for a rich dinner of poultry and takes them to a local theater performance acted by foxes dressed in feathered costumes. During their stay, he expresses his hatred for Aesop's fables for portraying foxes as cruel. Learning that Dorothy is a friend of Princess Ozma, King Dox asks her to procure an invitation for him to attend Ozma's upcoming birthday celebration. After receiving an invitation, he journeys across the desert to the Land of Oz and attends the royal gathering in the Emerald City, where he strutted around the Throne-Room and knelt at Dorothy's feet upon learning she is a Princess of Oz.

label: Appearance
value: Princess Langwidere possesses thirty different heads.
unit: Princess Langwidere possesses thirty different heads—one for each day of the month—stored in velvet-lined cupboards inside a private cabinet. Each head displays a distinct type of beauty, with varying hair colors, eye shades, nose shapes, and complexions, though none have gray hair or red eyes. Because she can alter her face at will, she continuously wears a simple white costume that suits all of her heads. The only constant identifier across her physical forms is a blood-red ruby key worn on a chain around her left wrist.

label: Personality
value: Langwidere is extremely vain.
unit: Langwidere is extremely vain and self-absorbed, spending much of her time playing the mandolin in a sitting-room lined with mirrors to admire her own reflection. She is often lazy, requiring her maid Nanda to assist her in standing up and walking. Her temperament changes depending on which head she wears; for instance, Head No. 17 carries a fiery, harsh, and haughty disposition that leads her to quick anger and rash decisions. She exhibits little interest in governing, spending state funds largely on herself while ignoring matters of importance.

label: History
value: Mombi lived on a round farm in the Gillikin Country.
unit: Mombi lived on a round farm in the Gillikin Country, where she was widely suspected by the local inhabitants of practicing illegal magic arts. In the past, she was secretly visited three times by the Wizard of Oz, who gave her the infant Princess Ozma to hide. In return, Mombi learned various magical tricks from the Wizard and transformed the young princess into a boy named Tip, whom she raised as her ward while forcing him to perform hard chores on her farm. Upon obtaining the Powder of Life from a crooked mountain wizard, Mombi tested the magical powder on Jack Pumpkinhead—a wooden dummy created by Tip to scare her—and brought the figure to life. After Tip escaped her farm, Mombi traveled to the Emerald City to assist General Jinjur and her rebel army. When Glinda surrounded the city demanding Mombi's surrender, Mombi attempted to deceive her by magically swapping forms with Jellia Jamb and later transforming herself into a red rose in the palace garden. Her trick was ultimately exposed when the Tin Woodman plucked the rose, leading to her capture. Brought before Glinda, Mombi was forced to speak the absolute truth under threat of death or the loss of her powers, confessing that she had transformed Princess Ozma into Tip.

label: Appearance
value: Nome King is a short, rotund man.
unit: He is a short, rotund man whose body, hair, flowing beard, and face match the exact gray-brown color of the rock throne he sits upon. His features appear kindly and good-humored, and his overall look reminds observers of Santa Claus, though devoid of the standard red coloring. He wears no crown, and his sole personal ornament is a wide, jewel-encrusted belt surrounding his waist.

label: Personality
value: The Nome King presents a jovial, pleasant demeanor on the surface.
unit: The Nome King presents a jovial, pleasant demeanor on the surface, frequently laughing so hard that he shakes like jelly and inviting visitors to sit and converse. He claims to be exceptionally kind-hearted and susceptible to wheedling rather than open threats or force. Beneath his merry exterior lies a deceitful, cruel, and hot-tempered nature. When thwarted or tricked, his face twists into terrible rage, and he takes delight in permanently trapping guests as decorative ornaments in his palace.

label: History
value: The Nome King rules a vast subterranean realm.
unit: The Nome King rules a vast subterranean realm situated beneath the earth's surface near the Land of Ev. After acquiring the Queen of Ev and her ten children, he transformed them into royal purple ornaments to decorate his subterranean palace. When Princess Ozma led an expedition to free the royal captives, he initially feigned hospitality and proposed a wager: each visitor could enter his palace to guess which objects were the transformed royals, but failing to guess correctly within eleven tries would result in their own transformation into decorative bric-a-brac. Through this trap, he successfully transformed Ozma, the Tin Woodman, twenty-six officers, and a private into ornaments. However, the yellow hen Billina discovered his secret while hiding under his throne, enabling the group to undo all of his enchantments. In the end, Dorothy captured his magical belt, stripping him of his power to transform opponents and leaving his plans foiled.

label: History
value: Ozma is the rightful hereditary ruler of the Land of Oz.
unit: Ozma is the rightful hereditary ruler of the Land of Oz, whose lineage traces back to rulers named 'Oz' or 'Ozma'. When she was an infant, the Wicked Witch Mombi transformed her into a boy so that no one would recognize her as the true Princess. She eventually escaped Mombi's power and reclaimed her throne with the assistance of Glinda the Good, defeating General Jinjur who had usurped power in the Emerald City. Later, during a quest in the realm of the Nome King, she was temporarily transformed into a green grasshopper by the king's deceitful magic. After being identified and restored to her natural form by Billina the yellow hen, she steadfastly assisted in recovering her enchanted companions, including the Scarecrow, Tiktok, and the Tin Woodman. Upon returning to the Emerald City, she welcomed Dorothy Gale and the Wizard of Oz, graciously appointing the Wizard as the Official Wizard of her kingdom. She subsequently hosted a grand birthday celebration attended by royal guests and notable figures from neighboring lands.

label: History
value: Polychrome danced on the rays of her father's rainbow.
unit: While dancing on the rays of her father's rainbow, Polychrome accidentally slid off the end and was left stranded on earth when the rainbow lifted away. Lost on a lonely road, she danced to keep warm and wept until she encountered Dorothy Gale, Button-Bright, and the shaggy man. Dorothy invited her to journey with them to the Emerald City, promising that Princess Ozma could help send her home. Along their journey, Polychrome enlivened the group with her music and dancing, though she encountered strange dangers such as the two-faced Scoodlers. Upon meeting Tik-tok and Billina in the Winkie Country, she was initially startled by Tik-tok's malfunctioning speech before continuing on toward Princess Ozma's birthday celebration.

label: History
value: Santa Claus attended Princess Ozma's birthday celebration.
unit: Santa Claus attended Princess Ozma's birthday celebration at the royal palace in the Emerald City, accompanied by a band of Ryls and crooked Knooks. Upon his arrival, he greeted Dorothy Gale, recognizing her from his Christmas Eve visits to her home. He also recognized Button-Bright and whispered a secret to the Wizard regarding where the boy lived. After greeting Polychrome and promising to notify her father, he placed his presents on the table for Princess Ozma. He spoke warmly to the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the shaggy man, and explained the duties of his accompanying Ryls and Knooks. Before disappearing, he borrowed the Saw-Horse to ride around the Emerald City and see its grand sights.

label: Appearance
value: The Saw-Horse is an artificial creature.
unit: The Saw-Horse is an artificial, quadrupedal wooden creature constructed like a carpenter's saw-horse. Its legs are stiff and lack knee-joints, causing its body to rock sidewise in a cradle-like pacing motion as it walks. It has knotty, bulging eyes, a short post hammered into its back to serve as a handhold, ears whittled out of tree bark, and legs shod with plates of gold.

label: History
value: The Saw-Horse was brought to life.
unit: The Saw-Horse was brought to life in the Land of Oz by the boy Tip using a magic powder. Upon first coming alive, he was astonished by his surroundings and spun in circles trying to see his own body. Because he initially had no ears, he could not hear commands until Tip whittled a pair out of tree bark and attached them, though one was immediately broken when he tumbled into a gopher hole. To enable Jack Pumpkinhead to ride him without wearing out his wooden joints, Tip hammered a wooden post into his back for a handhold.

value: The Saw-Horse proved brave during their travels.

He eventually met Jim, a real cab-horse, and introduced him to his friends the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger.

value: The Scarecrow wears a suit of faded blue clothes.

label: Goals
value: To help Dorothy Gale return to Kansas

label: History
value: The Scarecrow set out on a journey along the yellow brick road.
unit: The Scarecrow set out on a journey along the yellow brick road to seek brains from the Wizard of Oz in the Emerald City, joining Dorothy Gale on her quest to return to Kansas. Along the way, he welcomed the Tin Woodman into their traveling party and survived encounters with the Stinging Bees and Winged Monkeys sent by the Wicked Witch. He eventually became the monarch of the Emerald City, wearing a heavy golden crown and ruling from his throne. Upon meeting Jack Pumpkinhead, he believed they spoke different languages and called for an interpreter until he realized Jack's smiling mouth was carved that way. After being driven out of the Emerald City by rebels, he traveled with Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead upon the live Saw-Horse to seek aid from his friend, the Tin Woodman. At the Tin Woodman's palace, the Scarecrow's head was laundered and restuffed with his original brains, his clothes were pressed, and his crown was re-stitched before he set out to recapture the Emerald City.

unit: The Scarecrow set out on a journey along the yellow brick road to seek brains from the Wizard of Oz in the Emerald City, joining Dorothy Gale on her quest to return to Kansas. Along the way, he welcomed the Tin Woodman into their traveling party and survived encounters with the Stinging Bees and Winged Monkeys sent by the Wicked Witch. He eventually became the monarch of the Emerald City, wearing a heavy golden crown and ruling from his throne. Upon meeting Jack Pumpkinhead, he believed they spoke different languages and called for an interpreter until he realized Jack's smiling mouth was carved that way. After being driven out of the Emerald City by rebels, he traveled with Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead upon the live Saw-Horse to seek aid from his friend, the Tin Woodman. At the Tin Woodman's palace, the Scarecrow's head was laundered and restuffed with his original brains, his clothes were pressed, and his crown was re-stitched before he set out to recapture the Emerald City.

label: History
value: The Shaggy Man meets Dorothy while traveling.
unit: While traveling, the Shaggy Man meets Dorothy and shows her the Love Magnet given to him by an Eskimo. Deciding to take the seventh road together, he travels alongside Dorothy, Toto, Button-Bright, and Polychrome. During their journey, King Kik-a-bray transforms his head into a brown donkey head as a gift, forcing the group to seek the Truth Pond in the Land of Oz to restore his true form. Reaching the edge of the Deadly Desert, he uses the Love Magnet to summon Johnny Dooit, who constructs a sand-boat to transport the group safely across. Upon arriving at the royal palace in the Emerald City, he is given magnificent private apartments by order of Princess Ozma, where he bathes and dresses in luxurious shaggy apparel.

label: History
value: Tiktok befriended Dorothy Gale
unit: Tiktok befriended Dorothy Gale and saved both her life and Billina's life during past adventures. Later, Princess Ozma observed Dorothy traveling toward the Country of the Winkies in her magic picture. Because Ozma was busy preparing for her grand birthday celebration in the Emerald City, she dispatched Tiktok and Billina to welcome Dorothy and her companions. Upon meeting Dorothy's new companions—the shaggy man, Polly, and Button-Bright—Tiktok bowed politely, but his speech mechanism ran down mid-sentence, requiring Dorothy to wind him up under his right arm. Shortly afterward, his thought mechanism ran down, causing him to utter unintelligible babble until Dorothy wound him up again under his left arm. Once fully restored, Tiktok successfully conveyed Princess Ozma's invitation for Dorothy and her friends to proceed directly to the Emerald City.

label: History
value: The Tin Woodman originally was a human wood-chopper.
unit: Originally a human wood-chopper, the Tin Woodman lost his organic body piece by piece to an enchanted axe hexed by the Wicked Witch of the East, having each part replaced with tin by a local tinsmith. After losing his heart in the process, he traveled to the Emerald City with Dorothy Gale and the Scarecrow to seek a heart from Oz, who eventually placed a silk-and-sawdust heart in his chest. Following the defeat of the Wicked Witch of the West, he was chosen by the Winkies to rule as their Emperor in his tin castle. When the Scarecrow was deposed from the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman welcomed him, offered his Imperial Laundry, and joined the quest to restore his comrade. Later, during a court trial in Oz, he agreed to hide a piglet in his hat to assist the Wizard and save Eureka's life.

After losing his heart in the process, he traveled to the Emerald City with Dorothy Gale and the Scarecrow to seek a heart from Oz, who eventually placed a silk-and-sawdust heart in his chest. Following the defeat of the Wicked Witch of the West, he was chosen by the Winkies to rule as their Emperor in his tin castle. When the Scarecrow was deposed from the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman welcomed him, offered his Imperial Laundry, and joined the quest to restore his comrade. Later, during a court trial in Oz, he agreed to hide a piglet in his hat to assist the Wizard and save Eureka's life.

label: History
value: Tip lived in Gillikin Country
unit: Tip lived in Gillikin Country under the care of the witch Mombi. To startle her, he built a wooden figure with a carved pumpkin head named Jack Pumpkinhead and set it up along a bend in the road. Secretly watching Mombi, Tip witnessed her bring Jack to life using the Powder of Life obtained from a mountain wizard. After Mombi threatened him, Tip escaped her home with Jack, stealing the magical powder in a pepper-box. Using the powder, Tip animated a wooden Saw-Horse to serve as their mount, and later constructed and animated the Gump to escape dangers. Tip led his companions toward the Emerald City to meet the Scarecrow. Along the road, he encountered General Jinjur and learned of her Army of Revolt's secret plan to conquer the Emerald City. He later discovered that he was originally Princess Ozma, the rightful ruler of Oz, transformed into a mortal boy by magic, and was restored to his true form.

To startle her, he built a wooden figure with a carved pumpkin head named Jack Pumpkinhead and set it up along a bend in the road. Secretly watching Mombi, Tip witnessed her bring Jack to life using the Powder of Life obtained from a mountain wizard. After Mombi threatened him, Tip escaped her home with Jack, stealing the magical powder in a pepper-box. Using the powder, Tip animated a wooden Saw-Horse to serve as their mount, and later constructed and animated the Gump to escape dangers. Tip led his companions toward the Emerald City to meet the Scarecrow. Along the road, he encountered General Jinjur and learned of her Army of Revolt's secret plan to conquer the Emerald City. He later discovered that he was originally Princess Ozma, the rightful ruler of Oz, transformed into a mortal boy by magic, and was restored to his true form.

label: History
value: Toto accompanies Dorothy Gale on her travels.
unit: Toto accompanies Dorothy Gale on her travels through various magical lands, including the Land of Oz. During their early journeys to the Emerald City, he sleeps beside Dorothy at night while guarding her room with the Cowardly Lion. Unlike the inhabitants of Oz, Toto does not speak and communicates primarily through tail-wagging or barking. On later travels across unfamiliar lands, Toto enjoys running freely, chasing butterflies, and meeting Dorothy's new companions like Polychrome, the Shaggy Man, and Button-Bright. When confronted by dangerous hazards such as the hostile Scoodlers in the rock hollows, Toto crouches in fear between Dorothy's feet and whines as the party tries to pass safely.

label: History
value: Uncle Henry resided on a small farm in the middle of the flat Kansas prairies.
unit: Uncle Henry resided on a small farm in the middle of the flat Kansas prairies with his wife, Aunt Em, and his orphaned niece, Dorothy. When a cyclone struck their home, he ran to secure their farm stock while Dorothy was carried away inside the house. Due to years of relentless labor on his farm, his health suffered, leaving him weak and nervous. To recover and rest, he left Aunt Em to manage the farm while he traveled by ship to Australia to visit relatives, taking Dorothy along for company. After arriving in Australia, he spent time resting in Sydney, smoking his pipe, and later visited his relative Uncle Hugson at Hugson's Ranch in California.

label: History
value: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled the Western land of Oz from her castle.
unit: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled the Western land of Oz from her castle, having previously used the Winged Monkeys to drive out Oz and enslave the local Winkies. When Dorothy Gale and her companions entered her country to destroy her, she spotted them using her powerful single eye. She first blew her silver whistle to send a pack of forty great wolves to tear them to pieces, but the Tin Woodman slain them all. She then summoned a flock of wild crows, which were also defeated. Having exhausted her other options, she put on the magical Golden Cap and spoke its incantation to summon the Winged Monkeys for her third and final allowed time. She commanded them to destroy the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, capture the Lion, and bring Dorothy and Toto to her castle. Upon seeing the mark of the Good Witch's kiss on Dorothy's forehead and her Silver Shoes, the Witch realized she could not harm the child directly, so she forced Dorothy into kitchen slavery instead. However, Dorothy eventually threw a bucket of water over her during a confrontation, causing the Wicked Witch to completely melt away and freeing her captives.

label: History
value: The Wizard worked in Omaha.
unit: The Wizard originally worked in Omaha and performed balloon ascensions for Bailum & Barney's circus. Upon first drifting to the Land of Oz in his balloon, the people welcomed him as their ruler due to his initials. He oversaw the construction of the Emerald City and ruled it for many years using clever illusions and ventriloquism to make the populace believe he was a powerful magician. When Dorothy Gale and her companions arrived to request favors, he demanded they destroy the Wicked Witch of the West first. After Toto knocked over a screen in the Throne Room, his true nature as a common man and humbug was revealed. He satisfied Dorothy's companions by granting them their requested brains, heart, and courage through clever trickery. He then attempted to return to Kansas with Dorothy via a hot-air balloon, but the ropes snapped prematurely, leaving Dorothy behind as he floated away to Omaha. Finding his old friends gone or deceased upon his return, he rejoined the circus. During a balloon ascension, an earthquake caused him to fall into a chasm beneath the Earth, bringing him to the Land of the Mangaboos where he reunited with Dorothy and met Zeb. After journeying together through subterranean realms and facing various dangers, he arrived at the Emerald City. Princess Ozma welcomed him back, offering him a permanent home as the Official Wizard of her kingdom, which he accepted with emotional gratitude.

He oversaw the construction of the Emerald City and ruled it for many years using clever illusions and ventriloquism to make the populace believe he was a powerful magician. When Dorothy Gale and her companions arrived to request favors, he demanded they destroy the Wicked Witch of the West first. After Toto knocked over a screen in the Throne Room, his true nature as a common man and humbug was revealed. He satisfied Dorothy's companions by granting them their requested brains, heart, and courage through clever trickery. He then attempted to return to Kansas with Dorothy via a hot-air balloon, but the ropes snapped prematurely, leaving Dorothy behind as he floated away to Omaha. Finding his old friends gone or deceased upon his return, he rejoined the circus. During a balloon ascension, an earthquake caused him to fall into a chasm beneath the Earth, bringing him to the Land of the Mangaboos where he reunited with Dorothy and met Zeb. After journeying together through subterranean realms and facing various dangers, he arrived at the Emerald City. Princess Ozma welcomed him back, offering him a permanent home as the Official Wizard of her kingdom, which he accepted with emotional gratitude.

label: Appearance
value: The Woggle-Bug appears fully as tall as the Tin Woodman when standing upright.
unit: Standing upright, the Woggle-Bug appears fully as tall as the Tin Woodman, having attained an enormous size compared to ordinary bugs. He possesses a flat, round body that is glistening dark brown on the back and striped with bands of light brown and white across the front, supported by slender legs with upward-curling toes. His head features bulging black eyes, a nose ending in a curling feeler, and ears with miniature curling pigtail antennae on the sides. He wears a dark-blue swallowtail coat with yellow silk lining, a tight white duck vest, fawn-colored plush knickerbockers with gilt buckles at the knees, and a tall silk hat perched on his head.

label: Personality
value: The Woggle-Bug is intensely proud of his high level of education.
unit: The Woggle-Bug is intensely proud of his high level of education and vast erudition, frequently boasting that he is the most intelligent being in Oz. He considers himself a cultured gentleman, making polite bows and striving to impress others with his learning. He takes great pleasure in surprising people, strutting about after making brilliant remarks, and indulging in irresistible wordplays and puns. Despite his pomposity and tendency to display rudeness or condescending behavior, he displays humility when reprimanded or threatened by his companions.

unit: The Woggle-Bug is intensely proud of his high level of education and vast erudition, frequently boasting that he is the most intelligent being in Oz. He considers himself a cultured gentleman, making polite bows and striving to impress others with his learning. He takes great pleasure in surprising people, strutting about after making brilliant remarks, and indulging in irresistible wordplays and puns. Despite his pomposity and tendency to display rudeness or condescending behavior, he displays humility when reprimanded or threatened by his companions.

label: History
value: The Woggle-Bug was projected on a screen.
unit: While projected on a screen in a highly-magnified state, the Woggle-Bug bowed to the classroom pupils, which startled two girls into falling out a window. Taking advantage of the resulting chaos as the professor and students rushed outside, he calmly walked out of the schoolhouse and escaped while remaining in his magnified size. While wandering the countryside, he met Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, accepting their invitation to travel alongside them to the Emerald City. When the Saw-Horse broke its leg, the Woggle-Bug suggested amputating one of Jack's wooden legs to replace it. Throughout their journey, he frequently irritated his companions with puns and jokes until the Tin Woodman's axe-twirling warning prompted him to promise restraint. He joined the group aboard the flying Gump, riding along toward the South Country. Later, he came to reside in the Emerald City, where Princess Ozma appointed him as the Dean of the Royal College of Athletic Science. When meeting Dorothy and her companions in the palace, he proudly introduced himself before sitting down in a corner to read.

label: History
value: Zeb fell into a subterranean realm.
unit: Zeb fell into a subterranean realm alongside Dorothy, his horse Jim, and the Wizard following an earthquake. Together, they navigated through various strange underground worlds, surviving attacks by Gargoyles and facing judgment in distant kingdoms. After escaping the subterranean regions, they safely arrived in the Land of Oz. Upon reaching the Emerald City's Royal Palace, Zeb unharnessed Jim and bathed before changing into a velvet costume to dine with Princess Ozma. During the royal games, he competed in a wrestling match against a strong Munchkin who easily defeated him, and then engaged in a boxing match that caused the Munchkin to cry. Later, Zeb served as the starter for a race between Jim and the Sawhorse, calling the signal to begin. When Jim lost and kicked the Sawhorse in anger, Zeb rushed over to warn his horse to control his temper before the royal beasts could harm him. Following the festivities, he accompanied Jim back to the city while discussing their place in a fairy land.
